_comment: -p/--print: non-interactive, prints final response and exits.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): the model's own text
output only, no outer transport envelope. `--output-format json`
wraps the agent's answer inside a Claude CLI-specific envelope
object (duration_api_ms/session_id/usage/.../result/...) with the
actual workflow JSON nested as an escaped string inside the
envelope's `result` field -- WriterResult/ReviewerResult would
then parse the wrong (outer) JSON object and always see a missing
'status'/'verdict' field. text output has no such envelope; the
workflow prompt already instructs the agent to report its result
as a single JSON object on the LAST line of output (see
prompts.py), which is exactly what agent_results.py's
last-non-empty-line JSON extraction expects.
--permission-mode acceptEdits: auto-approve file edit/write tool
calls (the Writer role's whole job is CAN_EDIT_REPO within
allowed_files -- enforced separately by the orchestrator's scope
gate, not by this CLI flag).
--permission-prompts none: anything else that would need interactive
approval is auto-denied instead of hanging forever waiting for a
human who is not there (there is no human in a subprocess).
Prompt is appended as the trailing positional argument by
LocalCommandExecutor (prompt_via=arg), matching `claude`'s
`[options] [command] [prompt]` usage.
Separate invocation/process from the Writer, with its own reviewer
prompt (build_reviewer_prompt / build_closure_reviewer_prompt) that
explicitly instructs READ ONLY behavior.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): same reasoning as the Writer
above -- avoids Claude CLI's outer JSON transport envelope so
ReviewerResult.from_raw_output() parses the agent's own last-line
JSON verdict object, not the CLI's envelope.
--permission-mode plan: a read/inspect-oriented mode that does not
apply file edits.
--restricted: removes Bash/PowerShell/REPL/other code-running tools
and WebFetch, and ignores user/project/local settings files -- the
Reviewer never needs to execute code (targeted_tests/static_checks
are run by the orchestrator itself, not by the reviewer agent).
--disallowedTools Edit,Write,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit: explicit
defense-in-depth denial of every file-mutation tool, on top of
--permission-mode plan and --restricted.
--permission-prompts none: same non-interactive fail-closed reason
as the Writer.
-- (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): required end-of-options marker. --disallowedTools
takes a variadic list (<tools...>); without a terminator, the prompt
string that LocalCommandExecutor appends after this command array
(prompt_via=arg) is itself consumed as extra (bogus) disallowed-tool
entries instead of being read as the prompt, and the CLI then exits
with 'Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt
argument' -- confirmed via a real LocalCommandExecutor smoke run.
This CLI-level restriction is a second, independent layer on top of
the orchestrator's own pre/post git-state diff comparison in
orchestrator.py, which rejects the reviewer's verdict outright if the
repository was modified during the reviewer's execution -- so
read-only is enforced even if a future CLI flag change loosens the
options above.
